page.layout: One page of text in the centre, with the running head and page number at the top. Margin notes at the right, faint and partly illegible. Fragments of the facing page at the left edge. Signature at the foot.

p.i: trouersiæ notanda sunt quæ in Canone diximus, nempe Spurios tum esse admittendos ad locum & dignitatem aliquam in republ. cum ob singularem ingenii eminentiam & virtutem publica auctoritate magistratus legitimantur.

main_text.p: 7 Nutricum etiam habenda ratio est, & ferenda de iis leges publicæ; quandoquidem multa vel virtutis vel vitiorum semina suguntur cum lacte nutricis.
In Oeconomicis attigimus de lactatione infantum, nec placet hoc loco prolixius de eadem agere. Videant Politicæ studiosi Tolosanum lib. 14. cap.3.

8 Pro liberis, sive infantibus imbecillibus parentum pauperum, itemq; pro expositis princeps peculiaria loca & domos fundare debet, in quibus alantur & ad usum reip. instituantur, quas domos τροφεῖα vocamus.

p.i: Et sic de natiuitate subditorum: Sequitur sanitas, cuius considerandæ sunt causæ tum minus principales, tum principales.
Minus principales, sive instrumentariæ causæ Sanitatis subditorum sunt, tum Prouisores sanitatis, tum Medici.
Prouisores sanitatis sunt illi, quos tanquam adiutores suos Princeps constituit in ordinandis iis, quæ ad publicam sanitatem pertinent.
Prouisores sanitatis videat, ut munditiæ in ōnib. seruetur, atq; adeo ne quid putidū inprimis & fœtidū

page.notes: Marginal notes at the right, in a different and faint hand (reads roughly "Mas bon", "Nutrice", "bas ist", "Nutrege", "ncigt"), are handwriting or show-through and are not transcribed. The left strip shows the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "trouersiæ" (the word is worn), "suguntur" (possibly "sugantur"), and the Greek "τροφεῖα" (accents uncertain).
